id: title:Gilbert09:clarify the ga4 built in report name error

review.posthog_relevance: Clarifies warehouse source configuration UX for Google Analytics ingestion, distinguishing reserved built-in report names from custom report names.
review.reason: The change updates an error message and its corresponding test assertion to provide clearer guidance when a user attempts to name a custom report after a reserved built-in report. This is a localized, bounded improvement to user experience and documentation, not a systemic capability or critical reliability fix.
review.uncertainty: The actual benefit depends on the frequency of this specific naming conflict and the severity of user confusion, which cannot be verified from the code alone. No production incident or broader architectural change is demonstrated.

observations.limitations: Only supplied hunk IDs are cited. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: The error message for a custom report name conflicting with a built-in report was updated. The message now explicitly states the name is already a built-in report and instructs the user to choose a different name, rather than the previous message which said it was a built-in report and asked to choose a different name. observations.code_quote: f"'{name}' is already a built-in report you can select on the next step. "
observations.posthog_connection: This change improves the user experience for PostHog warehouse source configuration, specifically when setting up Google Analytics ingestion. It helps users distinguish between selecting a standard, pre-built report versus creating a custom report, potentially reducing configuration errors or confusion when a desired name is already reserved.
